documents.panels.explorerHint: Shows every document as a tree with the type of each value. Select a value to copy its path or to filter by it.
documents.panels.schemaHint: Lists every field path with its types and coverage, and marks fields that are missing in some documents or have mixed types.
documents.panel.needsProjection: This visualization shows tables. Add a projection step under the query to turn its documents into columns, or choose a panel for documents.
documents.panel.needsDocuments: This visualization shows documents, and the query answered with a table.
documents.tree.hint: Select a value to copy its path or filter by it.
documents.tree.keys: Arrow keys move through the documents. Right opens a field, Left closes it, Enter opens or closes.
documents.tree.copyFailed: The browser did not allow copying.
documents.tree.filtered: Added a filter on {path} to the query.
documents.drill.label: Where in the documents
documents.distribution.pathHint: A path as the schema shows it, for example items[].price. Empty shows the first numeric field.
documents.card.titlePathHint: The field whose value titles the card, for example name. Empty uses _id.
documents.pipeline.hint: Each stage is JSON, for example { “$match”: { “status”: “paid” } }. Database types use Extended JSON such as { “$oid”: “…” }.
documents.pipeline.noStages: No stages yet: the query returns the collection’s documents.
documents.pipeline.previewFailed: The preview could not be loaded.
documents.pipeline.previewNotDocuments: This stage does not answer with documents.
documents.pipeline.notStage: A stage is an object with one operator, such as { “$match”: { } }.
documents.pipeline.notArray: The pipeline is a list of stages: […].
documents.pipeline.writeStage: {stage} writes data; Kalzit only reads, so the server refuses it.
documents.pipeline.lastValid: Until it is fixed, the last valid version runs.
documents.find.limitInvalid: Enter a whole number above 0, or leave it empty.
documents.projection.title: Projection to a table
documents.projection.none: Time series, stat, bar and table panels need a table. A projection step turns each document into a row, with one column per field path.
documents.projection.active: Panels get a table with these columns instead of the documents. Remove the step to get the documents back.
documents.projection.name: Name of column {number}
documents.pipeline.macros: In a $match, {“$__timeFilter”: “ts”} keeps the dashboard’s time range, and “${name}” stands for a variable.
documents.pipeline.disabledNotSaved: {count} disabled stages do not run and are not saved with the query; they stay only while you edit.
documents.find.skipInvalid: Enter a whole number of 0 or more, or leave it empty.
